reasoning_traces.think:
The foundational structure of stimulus compounding hinges on physiological summation of excitatory potentials, where two independent components (s1 and s2) contribute additively to a total potential. This summation is modeled as \( \mathcal{S}(s_1, s_2) = s_1 + s_2 \). When these components are presented together as a compound, they undergo a transformation to isolated action, which introduces a generalization effect. Postulate 5 asserts that such a shift results in a 25% decrement in excitatory potential, expressed as \( \Delta E = -0.25E_r \). The transition from compound (š1) to isolated (s1) implies a change in neural representation, captured by the vectorial summation of afferent impulses. These primitives form a closed-loop system where habit strength evolves through additive neural inputs, modified by contextual abstraction and stimulus isolation. Failure modes arise when summation exceeds thresholds or when generalization reduces potential below activation levels.
